dimensions.assessment: Affects all visitors to federal recreational sites managed by the specified agencies on September 17, 2026.
dimensions.evidence: waive standard amenity recreation fees on September 17, 2026, for each visitor to each site managed by the Bureau of Land Management

dimensions.assessment: Visitors experience a minor financial savings by not paying entrance or standard recreation fees for a single day.
dimensions.evidence: designate September 17, 2026, as an entrance-fee free date on which admission is free to all visitors

dimensions.assessment: Results in a one-time, temporary reduction in fee revenue collected by federal land management agencies for that specific day.
A narrow directive ordering specific agencies to waive fees on a single calendar date in 2026.
dimensions.evidence: directs the Department of the Interior and the Forest Service to designate September 17, 2026, as an entrance-fee free date

dimensions.assessment: Limited strictly to a single day, September 17, 2026.
dimensions.evidence: designate September 17, 2026, as an entrance-fee free date

missing_information: The expected amount of foregone fee revenue is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill designates a single day, September 17, 2026, as fee-free for entrance and standard amenity recreation fees across National Park Service sites, public lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Reclamation, and the Forest Service. The effects are short-term and limited to visitors on that specific date.
